title: GLP-1 picks and shovels: the fill-finish and delivery-device capacity beneath the molecule
map_limitation: Five blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) The equipment layer that gates the ramp is mostly unlisted, so supplier-side EDGAR full-text search cannot reach it: Syntegon, OPTIMA, groninger, Bausch and Stroebel and IMA Group are private or have been taken private, and the largest dedicated sterile fillers are the same story, with Catalent sitting inside Novo Holdings and Vetter, Fareva, Recipharm and PCI Pharma Services all private. aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment therefore carries three listed names against an order book whose two largest owners publish nothing, and sterile-fill-finish-capacity carries five against a stage the originators largely perform in house. That is a finding about the chain, not a gap in the search. (2) The device platform layer is private in the same way: SHL Medical, Nemera, Owen Mumford and Phillips-Medisize file nothing, so the ticker list on autoinjector-and-pen-platforms is what is left after four of the layer's principals are removed. (3) Most listed names here file outside the SEC and reach this map through research rather than through full-text search: 1SXP.DE, GXI.DE, DAE.SW, YPSN.SW, SKAN.SW, KRN.DE, GETI-B.ST, MIKN.SW, BANB.SW, PPGN.SW, LONN.SW, SFZN.SW, AV.MI, SDZ.SW, NOVO-B.CO, 5214.T, 8086.T, 600529.SS, 0386.HK, 2359.HK, 207940.KS, RELIANCE.NS, SUNPHARMA.NS, CIPLA.NS, BIOCON.NS and PPLPHARMA.NS. Only GLW, XOM, WST, ATR, BDX, STVN, TMO, ATS and RDY are reachable that way, and STVN and RDY are foreign private issuers filing 6-K and 20-F rather than 10-Q, so the quarterly cadence the screen assumes does not exist for them. (4) Three quantities this thesis rests on are directionally sourced and quantitatively soft. Nobody discloses GLP-1 filling line utilisation, so capacity constrained for multiple years rests on one quantified lead time that belongs to a different stage (18 to 36 months for large-scale peptide synthesis capacity) and one qualitative statement (sterile lines take several years to design, validate and qualify). Nobody splits GLP-1 revenue by container format, so the syringe versus cartridge versus pen question the signal actually asks cannot be answered from any disclosure on this map; West's 18% of net sales and Stevanato's high value mix are the closest available and neither is broken out by format. And the qualification lock-in that makes a second supplier take years is asserted by every trade source opened this run and quantified by none: the nearest thing to a measurement is Datwyler beginning GLP-1 component supply in 2026 for a medicine launched years earlier. (5) The map cannot see substitution away from itself. The oral Wegovy tablet launched on 5 January 2026 and passed two million prescriptions in a quarter. A dose that ships as a tablet consumes no glass barrel, no plunger, no filling line and no pen, and no source opened this run sizes how much injectable volume it takes. That is the single largest risk to every link from position 4 to position 11, and it is recorded here rather than scored, because scoring it is the heat stage's job.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: The tubing market is repeatedly described around the same five names (SCHOTT AG, Corning, Nipro, Nippon Electric Glass, Gerresheimer). Two of the five are unlisted or foundation owned, so the listed slice understates concentration.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Within glass, none: a container closure system is approved against a glass type. Away from glass, cyclic olefin polymer barrels exist and are a real route around this link, which is why the criticality stops at HIGH.
capture_inputs.logistics_constraint: Tube is shipped globally and is not a regional pricing-power asset, unlike the cement link on tibet-mega-dam where hauling cost created the rent.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not resolvable from any source opened this run. Tubing sits inside larger groups at every listed name here, and none of them break it out, so the margin question passes to the heat stage as PENDING rather than as a fact.

impact.rationale: Real but diluted, and the supply response is already funded. GLP-1 is one driver among several named in the same sentence as monoclonal antibodies and mRNA vaccines, and the tubing market it lands in is a large slow-growing industrial pool rather than a squeezed one: 6.27% compound growth to 2031 is not the shape of a bottleneck. The reason it is not scored lower is that Type I borosilicate is not substitutable inside an approved container closure system, so tubing output does set a physical ceiling. The reason it is not scored higher is that three separate drawers have already committed melt capacity against that ceiling, including two billion vials a year from one North Carolina plant. Scored between the touched-and-diversified-away anchor and clearly-moved.

notes.text: THE THESIS WAS TESTED AND IT SURVIVES WITH TWO CORRECTIONS AND ONE WARNING. The signal names six unmapped layers: sterile fill-finish lines, ready-to-use vials and cartridges, autoinjector and pen assembly, elastomer stoppers and glass barrels, single-use bioprocessing consumables, and the qualification bottleneck. Five of the six are on this map as their own links and every one of them cites a dated source fetched this run. CORRECTION 1: the qualification bottleneck is not a stage, it is a property, and it could not be cited as a stage. Nothing found this run describes a qualification and validation SERVICES layer with its own dated economics; what the sources describe is qualification as the switching cost inside positions 4, 5, 7 and 9. It is therefore recorded in each of those links' capture_inputs and bottleneck notes rather than built as a link, and the map says so instead of padding. CORRECTION 2: single-use bioprocessing consumables could not be cited AT ALL for this chain. The only Sartorius material reachable this run was undated product pages, and no dated source opened this run ties sterile filtration or single-use assembly demand to GLP-1 fill-finish specifically. A stage I cannot cite is not a stage, so it was dropped and named here rather than carried on the map with a decorative citation. THE WARNING, and the most important thing this build found: the capacity story and the order books already disagree in two places. ATS, the one listed issuer that discloses a segment close to pen and autoinjector assembly equipment, reported life sciences revenue down $38.9 million or 9.3% year over year, total backlog down to $1,958 million from $2,139 million, and described its new life sciences bookings as being OUTSIDE autoinjector GLP-1 assembly equipment. And the only source opened this run that asked whether the $480 billion of pledged US reshoring had reached upstream equipment suppliers found them merely cautiously optimistic with sector share prices largely unmoved. Meanwhile the demand anchor's fastest-growing product is a tablet that needs none of this chain. A heat run that scores this map as a pure shortage story without pricing those three facts is scoring the press releases, not the chain. STAGES CHECKED AND NOT BUILT, with the reason each: single-use consumables and sterile filtration (no dated GLP-1-specific source, above); contract sterilisation services for ready-to-use formats (could not be separated from the converters' own in-house sterilisation by any dated source, so it is folded into ready-to-use-containment-formats, whose own citation states the converter performs washing, siliconisation, crimping and sterilisation); cold chain and 2 to 8 degree distribution (real, and no dated source found this run connects it to GLP-1 device volumes rather than to pharma logistics generally); needle and cannula supply (not researched to a dated source in the time available, and named here so the next pass knows it is missing, not absent); secondary packaging, labelling and serialisation (folded into device-assembly-automation, whose equipment sources cover inspection and packaging in the same order book); and cyclic olefin polymer resin as its own raw-material link (the polymer route is real and is named in the glass tubing link's substitutability, but every COP source reachable this run was an undated product page, so the feedstock link was narrowed to halobutyl rubber, which could be cited). ARCHETYPES: ARCH-001 applied three times (primary-containment-converters, aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment, device-assembly-automation) and it is the spine of this chain; ARCH-004 applied twice (pharma-glass-tubing HIGH, halobutyl-elastomer-feedstock MEDIUM, the same shape landing at two different criticalities exactly as the archetype predicts); ARCH-003 applied twice, once inverted at aseptic-filling-and-isolator-equipment where the order book owners are private, and once in its investable form at glp1-demand-anchor; ARCH-006 applied once at us-onshoring-tariff-response, wired in as an extra topological root, which is the fourth chain in the corpus to carry it and the second where it changed the map rather than decorating it. ARCH-002 checked and did NOT fire: there is no EPC or competitively bid civil layer on this chain, because the buildings are the customers' own. ARCH-005 checked and did NOT fire: no power or grid equipment layer is material here. ARCH-007 checked and did NOT fire: no semiconductor layer is material to a glass, rubber and spring chain, and the connected-device electronics that would carry one are a feature, not a stage. NO CONFLICT WITH THE ARCHETYPE LIBRARY was found on this build, so nothing is escalated.
